body.x: The Seoul Metropolitan City will operate Seoul Technology Pavilion at CES (Consumer Electronic Show) 2023, the renowned tech show to be held for four days next year from January 5th (Thurs) to 8th (Sun).
They will also operate the K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion, which will have over 50 startups simultaneously for the first time.

○ CES is the cutting-edge technology show held every January in Las Vegas, United States. Major global companies - like Samsung and Google - announce their visions for the company’s future, and startups from various countries showcase the innovative technology they developed to the global market.

○ Seoul is a city that was ranked 10th in global startup ecosystems by the Global Ecosystem Report 2022 published by Startup Genome, the international startup ecosystem evaluation institution. The institution praised Seoul as a city possessing outstanding startup infrastructure.
In this upcoming CES, the ‘Seoul Technology Pavilion’ will be implementing innovative technology related to ‘mobility’ and ‘ESG’ at the main exhibition hall of the Las Vegas Convention Center (LVCC).

It is the first time a pavilion operated by a country (city) will showcase at the main exhibition hall - usually an exhibition space for companies leading the global tech industry, such as Samsung or Microsoft.

As such, the number of attending companies and the space for the exhibition will increase. The ‘Seoul Technology Pavilion’ in the main exhibition hall (LVCC) is 165㎡ and will showcase six open innovation startups and companies from Seoul. The ‘K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion’ will be composed of 50 outstanding Korean startups over 473㎡ at Eureka Park, the exhibition hall for countries and startups.

○ The Seoul Technology Pavilion is a platform to introduce the cutting-edge technology of innovative companies and startups of Seoul to the global market and propose a vision of Seoul evolving with technology. The pavilion consists of a Theme Zone, which implements visionary towards the future and experiential elements, and a Tech Zone, which displays the innovative technologies of partnered companies and startups partnered.

○ In particular, a massive 3D screen (7M * 3M) will welcome visitors to the Theme Zone, which will display immersive 4D and 3D videos that show the vision for the future of Seoul. UAM, drones, self-driving cars, and eco-friendly technology represent exemplary anamorphic technologies, along with the future industries of Seoul evolving with technology with impact. In addition, through a partnership with Caliverse, the immersive metaverse-based K-Contents experience will awestruck visitors in various directions.

Through CES 2023, the city of Seoul aims to propose the future image of Seoul as a tech hub under the vision of ‘Smart Traffic City, Green City, Seoul’ and simultaneously support the global expansion of outstanding startups.

○ The main themes of the Seoul Pavilion in CES 2023 are Mobility and ESG - key fields for achieving Seoul’s policy vision and have been proposed for Seoul Vision 2030 as the strategic goals of Smart Traffic City Seoul, Green City Seoul. Seoul is taking active measures, such as establishing a new urban air mobility (UAM) system and preparing to implement carbon neutrality (Net Zero).

body.x: Accordingly, SBA plans to showcase the Seoul Technology Pavilion’s innovative technology in the fields of ‘Mobility and ESG’ through open innovation in connection with companies. The open innovation program (the 6th Seoul Innovation Challenge) will be held with four major Korean companies to discover six startups. These startups possess innovative technology in related fields and support expansion into the global market through technical collaboration, commercialization support, and joint CES exhibitions.

○ The ‘Seoul Innovation Challenge’ is a project to support the research and development (R&D) of technology in startups possessing innovative technology in new industries. The Seoul Business Agency (SBA) partnered with Lotte Chemical and S-Oil on the eco-friendly energy business. The SBA also partnered with the Korea Aerospace Research Institute and HANCOM InSPACE, leaders in the urban air mobility (UAM) business. At last, the SBA selected six outstanding startups that fit the technical tasks presented by each company.

Earlier, SBA established a system of cooperation with the Seoul Digital Foundation and the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups for the composition and operation of the K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion. The Seoul City-Ministry of SMEs and Startups Joint Pavilion collaborated for the first time at CES through the conclusion of a trilateral agreement. The selection of startups expands to 50 companies with systematically integrated services provided.

○ The exhibition areas for the outstanding startups selected by the K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion are ▴mobility ▴bio/healthcare ▴ESG ▴manufacturing and ▴data. The Joint Pavilion expects to draw more attention to Eureka Park with the scale of integration and expansion compared to the previous year.

○ The selected companies will receive one-stop integrated services, from pre-consulting for CES, on-site exhibition and interpretation, IR presentations, and follow-up management. The joint partnership conducted consulting training on companies to receive the Innovation Award given to companies possessing innovative technology and aesthetic design at the CES. With this, 17 companies succeeded in winning the CES 2023 Innovation Award.

In addition, SBA signed separate partnerships with the business groups of 4 universities (Kyung Hee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) and the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development to give support for the exhibition. They chose 50 university student supporters for close local support for the 50 exhibiting companies in the K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion.

○ The selected university students are set to be matched 1:1 with startups in their desired fields and taught about their matched companies in advance to improve their understanding of these companies. These measures will support the companies' business communication and preparation for the exhibition and on-site interpretation.

Hyunwoo Kim - the CEO of the Seoul Business Agency (SBA) - said, “While we plan to propose a future vision of Seoul evolving with technology with the world’s biggest IT expo, CES, as the stage, we also plan to actively support the expansion of innovative startups, which lead Seoul’s startup ecosystem, into global markets.”
